findings.evidence: "A copy of each update goes to the shared benefits folder the same day." (appears verbatim after both the reimbursement-log sentence and the equipment-catalog sentence)
findings.fix: Write a distinct sentence for each process, or confirm and state explicitly that both updates really do follow the same distribution rule.
findings.violation: The identical sentence is reused for two different processes on two different schedules, which reads as copy-pasted boilerplate rather than a verified fact about each specific update.

findings.evidence: "In addition, eligibility applies only to a dedicated home workspace the employee personally uses."
findings.fix: Replace "In addition" with a restrictive connector such as "However" or "Note that."
findings.violation: "In addition" signals an additional eligibility grant, but the sentence actually narrows eligibility (a restriction), so the connector misrepresents the logical relationship.

findings.evidence: "the portal saves a draft automatically every few minutes"
findings.fix: State the exact autosave interval, e.g., "every 5 minutes."
findings.violation: "Every few minutes" is too vague for a policy document to be a reliable operational detail (could mean 2 minutes or 10).

findings.evidence: "The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: Specify the trigger event and use consistent units, e.g., "three business days after the request is flagged incomplete."
findings.violation: The reminder's start point is undefined (after submission? after the request became incomplete?), and "three days" is unqualified while the prior sentence uses "business days," creating a unit mismatch.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: List the specific criteria or item categories that require more than a photo receipt.
findings.violation: "Most requests" implies exceptions but never identifies which requests need more than a photo, leaving employees unable to determine their own requirement.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person, e.g., "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This switches to second-person ("You"/"we") while every other section uses third person ("Employees," "The manager," "The finance office"), breaking voice consistency.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with a neutral connector like "Additionally," or start a new, unconnected sentence.
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies this rule parallels the prior sentence about condition/photo checks, but a per-category device limit is an unrelated restriction, so the connector is misleading.

findings.evidence: "the policy applies to one device per category per employee" vs. "The stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year."
findings.fix: Clarify explicitly whether one claim can include multiple categories/devices, or whether the per-category limit applies across multiple claims.
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions, second paragraph (compare Eligibility, first paragraph)
findings.violation: It's unclear whether multiple device categories can be claimed under a single yearly claim or whether this rule implicitly allows multiple claims per year, contradicting the stated one-claim-per-year limit.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Either add an actual definition of "stipend item" and how it relates to "claim"/"request," or rename the section to reflect its actual content (e.g., "Monthly Reconciliation Process").
findings.violation: A section titled "Terminology Notes" is expected to define terms, but it never defines "stipend item" or distinguishes it from "claim" or "request"; it just repeats the phrase.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form."
findings.fix: Convert to third person, e.g., "Employees record the stipend item on the request form."
findings.violation: This is another shift to second-person voice, inconsistent with the third-person voice used elsewhere (and inconsistent even within this same document's mixed usage).

findings.evidence: "Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review" vs. "The finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle."
findings.fix: Identify a single responsible party and a single, consistent timeline for releasing funds.
findings.location: Terminology Notes, first paragraph (compare Reimbursement Amounts)
findings.violation: Two different actors (Payroll vs. finance office) and two different timing rules (after a monthly review vs. within one pay cycle) are given for the same disbursement step, without reconciling them.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Remove this redundant paragraph or merge any new detail into the "How to Apply" section.
findings.violation: This duplicates the portal-submission process already described in "How to Apply" without adding new information, padding the document.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Remove the comma: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility and uploading the receipt."
findings.violation: The comma before "and" incorrectly separates two items in what should be a simple compound predicate, creating an awkward, ungrammatical list.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Merge this into "How to Apply" as the authoritative step list, or explicitly reconcile the two descriptions.
findings.violation: This contradicts/duplicates "How to Apply," which already describes the portal-driven step sequence but never mentions "confirming eligibility" or "uploading the receipt" as portal steps, leaving two inconsistent accounts of the request process.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison publishes the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Designate one owner and one update cadence for the equipment catalog and use it consistently throughout the document.
findings.violation: This contradicts Program Overview, which states the IT asset group (not the finance liaison) tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month (not the start of the fiscal year).

findings.evidence: "Once approved, the team schedules the reimbursement for the next pay cycle."
findings.fix: Consolidate into one authoritative description of who disburses funds and on what schedule.
findings.violation: This is a third, inconsistent account of who handles final reimbursement and when - it conflicts with "The finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle" (Reimbursement Amounts) and "Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review" (Terminology Notes).

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: Update "Approval Timeline" to include this finance review step and clarify its order relative to the manager's review.
findings.violation: This adds a second review step not mentioned in "Approval Timeline" (which describes only the manager's two-business-day review), leaving the overall approval sequence and ownership unclear.

findings.evidence: "The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Clarify whether multiple claims are actually permitted per year, and if not, remove or rewrite this rule to match the one-claim limit.
findings.violation: This rule implies multiple claims per employee could occur within a benefit year, contradicting the Eligibility section's statement that "the stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year."

findings.evidence: "The benefits team reviews the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: State one owner and one cadence for the equipment catalog once, and remove the duplicate/conflicting mentions elsewhere.
findings.violation: This is a fourth conflicting statement about equipment catalog ownership and cadence, disagreeing with both Program Overview (IT asset group, monthly) and Special Cases (finance liaison, fiscal year start).

findings.evidence: "Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Specify the document, e.g., "Staff can request a printed copy of the equipment catalog at any time."
findings.violation: "A printed copy" has no clear antecedent in this sentence (presumably the equipment catalog, but it is not stated), making the request ambiguous.
